whatThisIs: The single route-scoped hold carrier. The repository already carries two hold mechanisms and neither is route-scoped: ConsumerDeliveryRouteState (src/lib/rcap/render/consumer-delivery-control.ts) is a path-wide kill switch that can only disable the whole consumer delivery path, and the deploymentReadiness block in data/rcap-codex/release-readiness.json records configuration completeness for a deployment, not for a route. Neither can hold ONE route while its siblings keep operating. This record exists precisely to fill that gap: it is the single route-scoped hold carrier, consumed by the availability derivation in packet-route-resolver.
whatThisIsNot: Not a kill switch (that is ConsumerDeliveryRouteState), not a deployment-readiness record (that is release-readiness.json deploymentReadiness), and not a route-state mutator: a hold row makes a route unavailable at the availability derivation; it approves nothing, invalidates nothing, and never edits launch-graph, fulfillment-authority, or registry records.
authoredBy: Captain or owner, by hand, in a reviewed commit. No generator writes this file and no workflow commits to it. The nightly source monitor CREATES REVIEW TASKS that may lead a person to add a hold here; it never adds one itself.
consumedBy: The runtime availability layer (RM-1 / packet-route-resolver) reads this file read-tolerantly: a malformed file is treated as 'hold everything it cannot parse', never as 'no holds'. Verified by scripts/verify-rcap-route-holds.mjs (schema + release discipline + --mutations), wired into npm test.

rowShape.routeId: EXACT launch-graph pathwayKey, e.g. 'VT:expungement-of-criminal-history-record-13-vsa-7602'. Holds name exact routeIds only. A jurisdiction code ('VT'), a wildcard ('VT:*', '*', 'ALL'), or any other path-wide or jurisdiction-wide expression is refused by the verifier — jurisdiction-scoped permission is a documented anti-pattern in this repository, and jurisdiction-scoped holds would be the same defect inverted.
rowShape.reason: Why the hold exists, in prose a reviewer can act on.
rowShape.evidence: String or array of strings: review-task paths, issue URLs, monitor report references, decision-record paths.
rowShape.placedBy: Who placed it (person, not agent id).
rowShape.releasedAt: null while the hold is active; RFC3339 timestamp once released. Present on every row.
rowShape.reacceptance: null while active. A released row MUST carry { "reference": <repo path or record id of the reacceptance evidence — the fresh acceptance/verification record that justified release>, "note": <optional prose> }. A release without a reacceptance reference fails verification: routes come back through re-verified evidence, never through deletion of the hold.

rules: Holds are appended, released in place, and preserved: do not delete a released row — the row is the history of the outage.
One route may carry a MAINTENANCE_HOLD and a LEGAL_HOLD at the same time; two active holds of the same type on the same route are a duplicate and fail verification.
Placing or releasing a hold changes no other record. Availability is derived; route state, authority and registry records are untouched.
The response procedure for source changes is docs/rcap/EVERGREEN_ROUTE_MAINTENANCE.md.
